frontend.prompt:
实现范围说明（仅前端）：对所有会向后端发送/接收实体的前端模块（创建表单、编辑表单、列表/详情加载器、API 客户端序列化层、表单验证逻辑、错误展示）进行修改和测试。不要修改后端或假定未提供的后端细节；所有与后端契约有关的事实必须被明确保留或在前端以不变方式处理。

必须实现的契约与不变事实（前端必须显式遵守并保留现有实现）：
- 后端现在对“title”键拒绝接收：任何发送到后端请求的 JSON payload 中出现键名为 "title" 即会导致后端返回 422。前端必须保证不向后端提交包含该键的请求。
- 创建操作：name 字段为必填。更新操作：name 字段可省略。前端的表单校验规则必须反映这一点。
- 响应不变：后端响应仍会同时包含 title 和 name 字段。前端在接收并展示响应数据时仍要显示这两个字段（不可在接收时静默删除或忽略 title）。
- name 的类型/长度/null 限制保持不变：前端必须继续使用现有的关于 name 的类型、长度和可否为 null 的校验规则（不要在前端猜测这些具体数值；应依赖并复用当前已有的 name 校验配置或从后端契约文档/代码中读取现有值）。
- 禁止静默忽略旧键（title）：当前端接收到包含 title 的数据时，不得在 UI 或后续发送请求时自动删除或隐藏该字段而不告知用户。必须以可见方式呈现并要求显式操作以移除该字段再发送更新请求。

前端实现要点（具体可执行的任务清单）：
1) 序列化/请求构建层
   - 在所有构造发送给后端的请求的代码路径（create/update API 调用封装、通用序列化 helper）加入断言/防护：在最终发出请求之前，验证 payload 中不包含键名 "title"。若检测到 "title"，立即阻止发送并抛出/返回可供 UI 展示的错误信息（例如 error.code = "deprecated_key_present"，error.field = "title"）。
   - 不要仅在 UI 层删除键；在序列化层强制检查可以防止其他模块无意传递该键。

2) 创建（Create）表单
   - 保持 name 字段为必填（与现有类型/长度/null 约束一致）。实现或复用现有 name 验证逻辑，不要更改验证参数。
   - UI 不应提供向请求中注入 title 键的路径（例如删除 title 字段输入）。如果历史数据/模板包含 title，按第 4) 规则处理。
   - 在表单提交前再次运行序列化层的 title 检查，保证最终请求 payload 中无 title。

3) 更新（Update / Edit）表单
   - 在编辑模式下，name 字段变为可选：表单提交时允许不包含 name（但若用户填写则必须满足现有的类型/长度/null 约束）。
   - 当从后端加载实体用于编辑时，如果响应包含 title，必须在界面中可见地展示该字段并标注“已弃用/不再被接受”的提醒。UI 提供两个明确动作：
     a) “保留响应展示”——仅在详情视图中展示 title（不提交回后端）。
     b) “移除并提交”——若用户要提交更新（PATCH/PUT），用户需显式选择移除 title 或点击明确的“移除 title 并提交”按钮；移除操作应从要发送的 payload 中删除 title，然后通过序列化层再次确认没有 title 后再发起请求。
   - 严禁在后台悄无声息地删除 response 中的 title 并提交更新；任何移除都必须是用户可见且可操作的。

4) 接收/显示响应
   - 即便后端不再接受 title，响应仍会包含 title 和 name。前端在详情/列表/表单预填加载等场景必须继续展示 title 字段。
   - 在展示 title 的地方必须加注说明："注意：该字段已弃用，后端已不再接受；要更新，请先移除该字段后再提交。"。

5) 错误处理
   - 若后端返回 422，前端应检查错误响应是否与 title 有关（若后端在响应中指明字段，识别并突出显示）。展示友好的错误提示，例如："请求包含已弃用字段 'title'，后端拒绝处理。请移除 'title' 后重试。"
   - 不要在收到 422 后自动删掉 title 并重试请求；必须让用户知道并明确操作后重试。

6) 自动化测试与验收测试（前端侧）
   - 单元测试：对序列化/请求构造模块添加测试，覆盖以下情形：
     • payload 中含 title 时阻止发送并抛出指定错误
     • create 请求必须包含 name 校验（复用现有约束）
     • update 请求可不含 name，但若含必须满足约束
   - 集成/端到端测试：模拟后端响应包含 title 的场景，验证：
     • UI 能正确展示响应中的 title 且带有已弃用提示
     • 在编辑并尝试提交仍包含 title 的 payload 时，序列化层阻止发送并 UI 显示错误
     • 用户显式移除 title 并提交后，payload 中确实不包含 title 并且请求被发送
   - 错误路径测试：模拟后端返回 422（因 title），确保前端展示并阻止自动重试/自动清理。

7) 开发文档与代码注释
   - 在序列化/请求构造函数、表单处理器、API 客户端处添加注释，明确："后端不再接受 title，任何发送包含 title 的请求将返回 422；响应仍可能包含 title，展示但不得静默删除。"
   - 在变更说明/PR 描述中列出所有前端改动点和如何测试。

验收条件（前端交付需满足的检查项）
- 所有发送到后端的请求经过自动化检查，无一包含键名为 "title" 的字段。
- 创建表单在未填 name 时阻止提交并提示（使用现有的 name 约束）。
- 更新表单允许不填 name；若填写则遵循现有约束。
- 当从后端接收到包含 title 的响应时，UI 可见地展示 title 并标注已弃用；不会静默删除该键。
- 当用户尝试发送仍包含 title 的更新时，前端阻止请求并显示明确错误，且不会自动移除后重试。
- 单元测试/集成测试覆盖上述关键行为并通过。

补充实施建议（工程实践）
- 在序列化层加入显式断言/异常并在 CI 中开启检查，防止未来代码更改引入 title 到请求中。
- 对于历史代码路径（例如自动拷贝后端响应到编辑 payload 的逻辑），明确替换为“显示 -> 用户显式选择移除 -> 构造不含 title 的 payload”流程。

注意（必须遵守）
- 不要在前端实现中猜测或更改未提供的后端约束细节；对于 name 的具体类型、最大长度、是否允许 null 等参数，前端应继续使用现有实现中的值或读取来自后端契约/文档的确切值，不可自行更改。
- 不要静默忽略或删除响应中的 title；任何删除必须是显式且用户可见的操作。

交付清单（交付时应包含）
- 修改过的序列化/请求构造代码并含断言
- 修改过的创建和更新表单及 UI 文案（包含已弃用说明）
- 单元/集成/端到端测试代码覆盖上述场景
- PR 描述与变更文档，说明如何验证“不提交 title”规则

结束。

backend.prompt:
Scope: Implement backend-only changes for all endpoints that accept or return the resource object that currently uses the keys name and title. Do not assume endpoint paths, HTTP methods, database schema or error envelope shapes — read and use the existing API/server schema and error formats where indicated. The instructions below must be implemented exactly and cover validation, persistence/serialization, tests and documentation touches needed to satisfy the requirements.

1) Non-acceptance of "title" in requests (main rule)
- Reject any incoming request payload that contains the JSON key exactly named "title" in the resource object being submitted. This rejection must happen even if the request also contains a valid "name" key. The presence of "title" anywhere inside the submitted resource object (top-level or nested relevant objects/arrays for the same resource) must trigger rejection.
- Response to such requests: return HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. Use the existing API/server validation/error response format (do not invent a new envelope). Include a machine-readable indication that the error is because the client provided the forbidden key "title" (for example, the error should identify the field path "title" and state it is not accepted). Do not silently drop or ignore the key; explicitly fail.

2) Create vs Update semantics for "name"
- Create operations (POST/create endpoints): require the request to include the "name" key. If the "name" key is missing, validate and return the same validation error behavior/format currently used by your API for missing required fields (use HTTP status currently used for validation errors; if your system uses 422 for validation generally, follow that). Enforce the existing type, length and nullability constraints for name exactly as they are today — do not change these constraints.
- Update operations (PATCH/PUT/update endpoints): allow the request to omit the "name" key. If the client provides "name" in an update, validate it against the exact same type, length and nullability constraints that apply today. Do not change existing semantics for updates beyond this. If your API treats partial updates differently (PATCH vs PUT), apply these rules consistent with your current semantics.
- Important: Do not make any assumptions about what the current "name" constraints are. Read the current API/schema/validation rules and enforce them unchanged. Explicitly document in code/comments that constraints are unchanged and where they are read from.

3) Responses (output) — keep both keys present
- All responses that return the resource (create response body, update response body, GET single, GET list, and any other responses that serialize the resource) must continue to include both keys "name" and "title" simultaneously in the response JSON.
- The server must derive the response value for "title" from the authoritative stored value for "name" (i.e., title = name serialization alias). Implement this in the serialization layer so responses always set title to the same string as name. Do not accept client-provided title; always compute it from name on output.
- If your storage currently includes a separate title column/field, keep or remove it only after evaluating migration strategy; if it remains, ensure it is synchronized with name on write (see persistence rules below). If the storage does not have title, do not add a persistent title column solely for the sake of responses — mapping in serialization is sufficient.

4) Persistence and internal model
- Authoritative field for writes: treat "name" as the canonical field. On create or update, write/modify the canonical name field only after it has validated successfully.
- If there is an existing persistent "title" column/field in the datastore: when writing name, also write title = name to keep them synchronized. When reading, prefer the canonical name (or the most recent canonical source) and serialize both name and title as identical. If you choose to keep a separate title column, add tests to ensure they remain identical after writes.
- If there is no title column, do not create persistent title data unnecessarily; simply compute and include title in the API serialization layer.

5) Validation behavior / error handling specifics
- Implement explicit detection logic that scans the payload for the exact key string "title" within the resource object(s). This must be implemented at the validation layer before any downstream write logic executes.
- When the forbidden key is present: immediately return 422 with the existing API's validation error response structure, identifying the offending field as "title" and a short message that the key is not accepted in requests. Do not proceed with any further validation or persistence for that request.
- For missing/invalid "name" in create requests: return existing-format validation errors. For invalid/invalid-on-update name: return existing-format validation errors.

6) Tests (unit + integration)
Add tests that prove the new behavior and preserve old constraints: at minimum implement the following test cases for each relevant endpoint type (create, update, get, list):
- Create: payload contains only title -> assert 422 and error identifies title key.
- Create: payload contains title and name -> assert 422 and error identifies title key (even though name present).
- Create: payload missing name (and no title) -> assert validation error as current behavior.
- Create: payload has valid name -> success (status as current API returns for creation), response JSON includes both name and title and their values are identical.
- Update: payload contains only title -> assert 422.
- Update: payload contains title and name -> assert 422.
- Update: payload omits name (and no title) -> success, response includes name and title (unchanged from prior state).
- Update: payload provides valid name -> success, response includes updated name and title matching.
- Verify that serialized GET/list responses include both keys name & title with identical values.
- If storage contains a title column, add tests to assert that after create/update both storage fields are identical.

7) Documentation and API spec
- Update the public API documentation and machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI/JSON Schema/other canonical schema you maintain) to state: "title" is not accepted in requests and any occurrence will result in HTTP 422; responses will continue to include "title" as a read-only alias for "name".
- In the schema/published contract, mark title as read-only (or server-only) in request schemas so it cannot be submitted by clients.
- Keep the documented constraints for name unchanged; reference the existing schema for exact type/length/nullability values.

8) Backward-compatibility and rollout notes
- Communicate to integrators that any request containing title will now be rejected with 422; clients must stop sending title in requests. Provide migration guidance: if a client previously sent title, they must send the same value as name under the name key now.
- Implement monitoring/metrics around 422 responses caused by the presence of title to help detect clients that still send the deprecated key.

9) Implementation checklist for engineers (concrete tasks)
- Locate request validation middleware/validators for the resource and add an explicit check for the presence of "title"; return 422 using existing error format if present.
- Ensure create handlers enforce required name; re-use existing validation rules for type/length/nullability unchanged.
- Ensure update handlers allow omission of name and validate if present, enforcing existing rules.
- Update serialization/DTO/response mappers to always include both name and title, with title derived from name.
- If the persistence layer contains a title field and you choose to keep it, update persistence code so writes keep title==name. If you remove the column, plan and execute a migration out of band (do not change behavior in this ticket without migration plan).
- Add comprehensive unit/integration tests listed above.
- Update API docs/spec to mark title as read-only in responses and forbidden in requests.

10) Explicit constraints and preserved facts (must be preserved exactly)
- The following facts are preserved and must be enforced exactly as currently defined in your system (do not change):
  - The type, maximum/minimum length, and nullability constraints that apply to the "name" field remain unchanged. Do not alter these values; instead, read and re-use the existing schema/validator configuration.
  - The server must not silently ignore previously-accepted keys: if clients send the old key "title" the server must return 422 rather than silently dropping the key.
  - Responses must continue to include both keys "title" and "name" together.

11) Notes and cautions
- Do not assume other teams will change their clients; therefore make the behavior explicit and detectable (error message and metrics).
- Do not invent new error formats or HTTP status codes beyond what your API currently uses for validation errors; if the current validation error status is 422, use 422. If different, use the existing validation response convention but ensure the behavior (immediate failure on title key) holds.
- Do not use undocumented historical details. Where the instructions require knowledge about existing constraints or error envelopes, read them from the current codebase/spec and re-use them unchanged.

Deliverables after implementation: updated validators, updated response serializers, automated tests demonstrating the new rejection rule and response behavior, and updated API docs/spec stating that title is server-only (read-only) and will cause 422 if submitted.
